name: Group totals and averages
question: How does {value_col} vary across {group_col} segments?
sql: SELECT {group_col} AS group_value, COUNT(*) AS row_count, SUM({value_col}) AS total_value, AVG({value_col}) AS avg_value FROM {dataset} GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY total_value DESC
rationale: Totals, averages and row counts per segment show where a measure concentrates and which groups behave differently.

name: Concentration (shares and HHI)
question: How concentrated is {value_col} across {group_col} (top shares and HHI)?
sql: WITH grouped AS (SELECT {group_col} AS group_value, SUM({value_col}) AS group_total FROM {dataset} WHERE {value_col} IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1), shares AS (SELECT group_value, group_total, group_total / SUM(group_total) OVER () AS share FROM grouped) SELECT group_value, group_total, share, SUM(POWER(100.0 * share, 2)) OVER () AS hhi FROM shares ORDER BY group_total DESC LIMIT 25
rationale: Per-group shares plus the Herfindahl-Hirschman Index (sum of squared percentage shares) quantify how dependent the total is on a few groups. HHI definition: https://www.justice.gov/atr/herfindahl-hirschman-index

params.name: group_col
params.description: Categorical column whose concentration is measured.

params.name: value_col
params.description: Numeric column whose total is shared out.

name: Missing-value audit by segment
question: Which {group_col} segments have the most missing {target_col} values?
sql: SELECT {group_col} AS group_value, COUNT(*) AS row_count, COUNT(*) - COUNT({target_col}) AS missing_rows, 1.0 - COUNT({target_col}) * 1.0 / COUNT(*) AS missing_rate FROM {dataset} GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY missing_rate DESC, row_count DESC
rationale: Missing data is rarely uniform; grouping the null rate by a segment column shows whether gaps cluster in specific slices (missing-value profiling as popularized by EDA report tools, e.g. https://github.com/ydataai/ydata-profiling).

params.name: target_col
params.description: Column whose missing values are audited.

params.name: group_col
params.description: Segment column to break the null rate down by.

name: Duplicate key audit
question: Are there duplicate {key_col} values that may inflate counts?
sql: WITH counted AS (SELECT {key_col} AS key_value, COUNT(*) AS occurrence_count FROM {dataset} WHERE {key_col} IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1) SELECT key_value, occurrence_count FROM counted WHERE occurrence_count > 1 ORDER BY occurrence_count DESC, key_value LIMIT 50
rationale: A key column that repeats silently inflates joins and aggregate counts; listing the repeated key values sizes the problem before any downstream analysis.

params.name: key_col
params.description: Column expected to identify one row or entity.

name: IQR outlier count
question: How many {value_col} values fall outside the 1.5 * IQR fences?
sql: WITH bounds AS (SELECT quantile_cont({value_col}, 0.25) AS q1, quantile_cont({value_col}, 0.75) AS q3 FROM {dataset}) SELECT COUNT(*) AS outlier_rows, (SELECT COUNT({value_col}) FROM {dataset}) AS non_null_rows, MIN(bounds.q1 - 1.5 * (bounds.q3 - bounds.q1)) AS lower_fence, MIN(bounds.q3 + 1.5 * (bounds.q3 - bounds.q1)) AS upper_fence FROM {dataset}, bounds WHERE {value_col} < bounds.q1 - 1.5 * (bounds.q3 - bounds.q1) OR {value_col} > bounds.q3 + 1.5 * (bounds.q3 - bounds.q1)
rationale: Counts rows outside Tukey's fences (quartiles -/+ 1.5 * IQR), the classic robust screen for candidate outliers in exploratory data analysis.

name: Monthly trend
question: How do {value_col} totals evolve month by month over {date_col}?
sql: SELECT date_trunc('month', CAST({date_col} AS TIMESTAMP)) AS month_start, COUNT(*) AS row_count, SUM({value_col}) AS total_value, AVG({value_col}) AS avg_value FROM {dataset} WHERE {date_col} IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
rationale: Truncating to calendar months smooths daily noise and exposes trend and seasonality in a measure.

params.name: date_col
params.description: Date or datetime column to bucket by month.

name: Category distribution
question: How are rows distributed across {category_col} categories?
sql: SELECT {category_col} AS category_value, COUNT(*) AS row_count, COUNT(*) * 1.0 / SUM(COUNT(*)) OVER () AS share FROM {dataset} GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY row_count DESC LIMIT 30
rationale: Category frequencies with shares reveal dominant and rare classes before any deeper segmentation.

name: Numeric quantile summary
question: What is the distribution profile of {value_col} (quantiles, mean, spread)?
sql: SELECT COUNT({value_col}) AS non_null_rows, MIN({value_col}) AS min_value, quantile_cont({value_col}, 0.05) AS p05, quantile_cont({value_col}, 0.25) AS p25, quantile_cont({value_col}, 0.50) AS median_value, quantile_cont({value_col}, 0.75) AS p75, quantile_cont({value_col}, 0.95) AS p95, MAX({value_col}) AS max_value, AVG({value_col}) AS mean_value, STDDEV_SAMP({value_col}) AS stddev_value FROM {dataset}
rationale: Quantiles plus mean and standard deviation summarize location, spread and skew of a numeric column in one row, without plotting.

name: Pareto cumulative share
question: Which {group_col} groups account for the bulk of {value_col}?
sql: WITH grouped AS (SELECT {group_col} AS group_value, SUM({value_col}) AS group_total FROM {dataset} WHERE {value_col} IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1) SELECT group_value, group_total, SUM(group_total) OVER (ORDER BY group_total DESC, group_value ROWS UNBOUNDED PRECEDING) AS running_total, SUM(group_total) OVER (ORDER BY group_total DESC, group_value ROWS UNBOUNDED PRECEDING) / SUM(group_total) OVER () AS cumulative_share FROM grouped ORDER BY group_total DESC, group_value LIMIT 50
rationale: Ranking groups by contribution with a cumulative share shows whether a few groups drive most of the total (Pareto / 80-20 screening).

params.name: value_col
params.description: Numeric column contributed to the total.

name: Month-over-month change
question: How does monthly {value_col} change month over month along {date_col}?
sql: WITH monthly AS (SELECT date_trunc('month', CAST({date_col} AS TIMESTAMP)) AS month_start, SUM({value_col}) AS total_value FROM {dataset} WHERE {date_col} IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1) SELECT month_start, total_value, total_value - LAG(total_value) OVER (ORDER BY month_start) AS absolute_change, (total_value - LAG(total_value) OVER (ORDER BY month_start)) / NULLIF(LAG(total_value) OVER (ORDER BY month_start), 0) AS relative_change FROM monthly ORDER BY month_start
rationale: Month-over-month absolute and relative deltas expose acceleration, slowdown and one-off spikes that a plain trend line hides.

params.name: date_col
params.description: Date or datetime column defining the monthly series.

name: Two-dimension cross tabulation
question: How does the {category_col} mix differ across {group_col} segments?
sql: SELECT {group_col} AS group_value, {category_col} AS category_value, COUNT(*) AS row_count, COUNT(*) * 1.0 / SUM(COUNT(*)) OVER (PARTITION BY {group_col}) AS share_within_group FROM {dataset} GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1, 3 DESC LIMIT 100
rationale: A two-way count table with within-group shares shows how a categorical mix shifts across segments.

params.name: category_col
params.description: Inner category column whose mix is compared.

name: Cardinality and imbalance audit
question: Is {target_col} nearly constant or dominated by a single value?
sql: WITH freq AS (SELECT {target_col} AS observed_value, COUNT(*) AS occurrence_count FROM {dataset} WHERE {target_col} IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1) SELECT COUNT(*) AS distinct_values, SUM(occurrence_count) AS non_null_rows, MAX(occurrence_count) * 1.0 / SUM(occurrence_count) AS top_value_share FROM freq
rationale: Distinct-value count and the top value's share flag near-constant or heavily imbalanced columns (alert categories popularized by profiling tools, e.g. https://github.com/ydataai/ydata-profiling).

params.name: target_col
params.description: Column audited for cardinality and imbalance.
